questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: New research on how our lifestyle can help us age well
Why grey hair and wrinkles appear
The life of the oldest person ever
How to cook Mediterranean food
questions.why: They hear new research offering advice on how to stay healthy as we get older.

questions.q: According to Professor Sarah Harper, what did experts believe ten years ago?
options: That diet was the only important thing
That we could stop ageing completely
That ageing was all about our cells
That loneliness caused most illness
questions.why: She says 10 years ago we would have thought, 'Yes, it's all to do with our cells.'

questions.q: What did a recent paper find about ageing?
options: It is about 90% decided by the genes we are born with
About 60% of it can be controlled by how we live
It happens faster in cities
It stops after the age of 80
questions.why: She says a paper found 60% of our ageing can be controlled by how we live.

questions.q: What did the twin studies show?
options: Twins always age at the same speed
Twins who eat more fish and vegetables live longer than other twins
Twins are healthier than other people
Twins with a positive attitude had better health later in life
questions.why: She says if you're positive, you have far greater health in later life than if you're negative.

questions.q: What does Sarah Harper say about loneliness?
options: It is only a problem in cold countries
It mainly affects young people
It has little effect on health
It can be as harmful as smoking
questions.why: She says loneliness can have the same impact as smoking in the statistics.

questions.q: Apart from food, what else is part of the Mediterranean lifestyle, according to Sarah?
options: Working long hours
Being outside more and eating meals together
Sleeping in the afternoon
Living alone in the countryside, far from busy cities
questions.why: She mentions exercise from being outside more and communal meals.

questions.q: What does Sarah say is changing a little in these countries?
options: Families living together in multigenerational homes
People eating fresh fish and vegetables almost every day
The warm climate
People exercising outdoors
questions.why: She says they tend to live in multigenerational households, but 'that is changing a bit'.

questions.q: What does Beth suggest people who don't live near the Mediterranean can do?
options: Move to a warmer country somewhere near the Mediterranean
Eat only vegetables
Stay positive and keep in contact with other people
Live with their grandparents
questions.why: She says a positive attitude and social interaction are two things we can all do to age well.
